analysis.title: United Parcel Service Inc. (UPS): First Take: 3Q26 EPS Ahead on U.S. and International EBIT; FY 2026 Outlook Raised on Beat; Buy
key_insights: UPS reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $1.69 versus GS/Visible Alpha consensus of $1.62/$1.63, up 17% y/y.

Domestic revenue per piece (RPP) grew 6.1% versus cost per piece (CPP) growth of 5.3%, an 84bp spread inside the company's 50-100bp guide. GS reads this as the result of actions taken alongside the Amazon volume drawdown, and a possible sign of better Domestic profitability over 2H on a y/y basis.

Domestic margin was 7.0%, in line with GS and consensus and at the company's 7% target, despite higher fuel prices in the quarter. Domestic EBIT of $1,034mm was 4% above GS's forecast, helped by slightly better volume, which GS says likely points to some growth in core volumes ex-Amazon.

International margin was 14.9% versus 13.5% for GS and consensus, above the company's 13%-14% guided range. International EBIT was $746mm versus $666mm GSe. International yield rose 15.1% y/y versus +12.4% GSe, while volume fell 8.7% versus -6.0% GSe.
Supply Chain Solutions EBIT was $274mm, 9% below GSe of $302mm, with a margin of 9.2% versus 10.8% GSe, despite revenue 6% above forecast.

FY2026 guidance was raised: revenue to $92.6B from ~$91.2B (GSe $91.9B, VA consensus $91.6B), EBIT to $8.75B (~9.4% margin, down from 9.5% previously), EPS to ~$7.28 from $7.22, and FCF to $6.1B. The EPS raise is roughly the size of the 3Q beat.
Capex (~$3.0B), dividend payments (~$5.4B, subject to Board approval) and the effective tax rate (~23.0%) were reaffirmed.

GS calls this the start of UPS's 'prove it' story after the Amazon drawdown completed in 2Q26, saying higher-revenue-quality packages are translating to a reasonable Domestic margin, which it expects to be positive for the shares.
GS maintains Buy with a $132 12-month price target (15.5x P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS of $8.55). The stock closed at $100.32 on 26 Oct, implying 31.6% upside.

Key topics for the 8:30am ET call: parcel demand and volume growth ex-Amazon, B2B recovery, Amazon glide-down versus cost takeout, Domestic margin direction, headcount reductions, the Ground Saver contract with USPS, tariff and geopolitical impacts, and International margin.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $1.69 beat consensus of $1.62-1.63 and FY26 EPS guidance was raised to ~$7.28. GS sees the quarter as early proof that the post-Amazon Domestic margin can hold.

earnings_insights: UPS 3Q26 adjusted (recurring) EPS was $1.69 as reported on 10/27/26, versus GS estimate $1.63 and GS/Visible Alpha consensus $1.62-1.63. Reported EPS was $1.37 (GSe $1.63) after a $279mm extraordinary loss.
Total revenue was $22.85B versus GSe $22.0B (+4%) and consensus $22.18B (+3%). Operating income was $2,054mm versus GSe $1,966mm and consensus $1,978mm. Consolidated margin was 9.0% versus GSe 8.9%.
Domestic revenue was $14.87B (GSe $14.26B, consensus $14.38B). Yield grew 6.1% y/y versus +4.8% GSe, and volume fell 3.3% y/y versus -4.3% GSe and -3.3% in 2Q.
International revenue was $5.0B versus GSe $4.93B. Supply Chain & Freight revenue was $2.98B versus GSe $2.81B.
FY2026 company guidance: revenue $92.6B, EBIT $8.75B, EPS ~$7.28 (from $7.22), FCF $6.1B. GS's pre-print FY26E EPS was $7.20 and its 4Q26E EPS was $2.76.
GS is awaiting call details on volume and margin cadence for 4Q26 and will update its EPS outlook after the 8:30am call.
risk_factors: Material economic slowdown, including tariff impacts on global freight flows.
New entrants, peak season disruptions, and the ability to absorb higher costs from the new contract.
Unionized labor force and execution of Network of the Future.
Execution and incorporation of the new USPS contract, including a potential new GroundSaver delivery contract.
Remaining Amazon volumes and whether they exit after 2H26, and the ability to cut costs in time to match the Amazon exit.
Execution of the multi-year network reconfiguration and efficiency cost takeout plan.
geopolitical: The report lists geopolitical events and tariff impacts on international freight as questions for the earnings call.
